scope: Proposition 1.3 (Standard properties of nested CLE4) of the manuscript “The curve scaling limit of half-plane double dimers” (preprints/The-curve-scaling-limit-of-half-plane-double-dimers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 226 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2e1bcd39145db94c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: After conformal transport to the disk, nested CLE4 consists almost surely of pairwise disjoint simple loops contained in the open disk. There are finitely many loops of diameter greater than any positive number. Every fixed interior point is almost surely off all loop traces and is surrounded by infinitely many successive nested loops.
